prerequisite_diagnostic.purpose: Distinguish between flat and solid shapes.

items.question: Which of these can you hold in your hand like a ball: a square drawn on paper or a wooden cube?
items.remediate_if: Treats 2D drawings and 3D objects as the same.

lessons.title: Faces, Edges, and Vertices
lessons.objective: Learner can count parts of a 3D shape.
teach: A 3D shape has 3 parts you can touch:
1. Face: The flat surface (like the side of a box).
2. Edge: The line where two faces meet.
3. Vertex: The corner point where edges meet (plural: vertices).

worked_example.prompt: Count Faces, Edges, and Vertices for a Cube.
worked_example.method: 1. Faces: Top, bottom, front, back, left, right = 6. 2. Edges: 4 on top, 4 on bottom, 4 vertical = 12. 3. Vertices: 4 on top, 4 on bottom = 8.

lessons.checkpoint: How many vertices does a pyramid with a square base have?

lessons.title: Nets: Flattening a Solid
lessons.objective: Learner can identify which 2D pattern makes a 3D shape.
teach: A 'Net' is a flat skeleton of a 3D shape.
If you cut open a cardboard box and lay it flat, that is its net.

worked_example.prompt: What does a net with 6 identical squares make?
worked_example.method: 1. Squares are identical faces. 2. 6 faces are needed for a cube. 3. Result = Cube.

lessons.checkpoint: Can 4 triangles and 1 square make a square pyramid?

lessons.title: Views of a Solid
lessons.objective: Learner can identify a shape from top, side, and front views.
teach: An object looks different depending on where you stand.
Front View: Looking straight at it.
Side View: Looking from the left or right.
Top View: Looking down from above (also called Plan view).

worked_example.prompt: A cylinder (like a soda can) is standing up. What are its views?
worked_example.method: 1. Front/Side: You see a rectangle. 2. Top: You see a circle.

lessons.checkpoint: If you look at a ball from the top, what shape do you see?

items.question: What is another name for the 'corners' of a 3D shape?
items.explanation: Vertices are the points where edges meet.

items.question: How many edges does a cube have?
items.explanation: A cube has 12 edges (4 top, 4 bottom, 4 vertical).

items.question: Which 3D shape can be made from a net of two circles and one rectangle?
items.explanation: A cylinder has two circular bases and a curved surface that flattens into a rectangle.

items.question: If you look at a cube from the top, what shape do you see?
items.explanation: All faces of a cube are squares, so any view (top, front, side) is a square.

items.question: A solid has 4 faces and 4 vertices. How many edges does it have? (Hint: F+V-E=2)
A triangular pyramid is also known as a:
items.explanation: A tetrahedron is a pyramid with a triangular base.

items.question: How many squares are needed to form the net of a cube?
items.explanation: A cube has 6 faces, so its net must have 6 squares.

items.question: An oblique sketch of a cube does not show:
items.explanation: Oblique sketches show the general shape but the lengths are not always proportional.

items.question: What is the cross-section of a carrot when cut horizontally?
items.explanation: Cutting a cone-like shape (carrot) horizontally gives a circular cross-section.

items.question: Which of these is a 2D shape?
items.explanation: A circle is flat (2D), while others are solids (3D).

misconception_remediation.diagnostic: Ask the learner to point to an edge on a box.
repair: Use a box. Run a finger along the 'line' (edge).
Explain that edges are lines and vertices are dots.
misconception_remediation.exit_criterion: Learner correctly counts edges vs vertices on a new shape.

misconception_remediation.diagnostic: Show a net of 6 squares in a straight line.
repair: Explain that when folded, some squares will overlap and one side will be empty.
Demonstrate folding to show it doesn't close the cube.
misconception_remediation.exit_criterion: Learner correctly identifies which of 3 patterns can form a cube.

misconception_remediation.diagnostic: Check if learner thinks a cube has only 3 faces because only 3 are visible in a drawing.
repair: Use a real box to show the back and bottom faces.
Explain that 3D drawings 'hide' some parts from view.
misconception_remediation.exit_criterion: Learner correctly identifies the total count of faces for a drawn solid.
